name: Vermont
agency: Vermont Department of Motor Vehicles (Agency of Transportation)
permitAge: 15 (handbook p. 12; parent or guardian signs under 18; clean driving record for the previous 2 years)

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours, at least 10 at night (night = 30 min after sunset to 30 min before sunrise), on top of the 6 behind-the-wheel hours of driver education (handbook pp. 13-14, 20)
teen.holdPermit: At least 1 year, with no permit recall/suspension in the last 6 months (handbook p. 13, 20)
teen.passengerLimit: Junior license: first 3 months alone or with a licensed parent/guardian, instructor, or licensed person 25+; months 4-6 may also carry immediate family (siblings and parents); never more passengers than seat belts (handbook pp. 15, 20-21). Violation = 90-day recall (23 V.S.A. 607a, 614(c)).
teen.phone: All drivers: no hand-held portable electronic device use, even when stopped in traffic (handbook p. 55; 23 V.S.A. 1095b; hands-free allowed for 18+). Under 18: no device use at all, hands-free included, except emergency contact (23 V.S.A. 1095a).

bac.under21: 0.02 (handbook p. 52; since 2025-07-01 under 7 V.S.A. 656, 23 V.S.A. 1216 repealed: first offense 90-day suspension, 180 days if youth program not completed)

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 against the Vermont Driver's Manual VN-007 07/2024 (cover says 2025; PDF dated 2024-11-18). Printed page = PDF page minus 1.
Knowledge test: online at mydmv.vermont.gov, 20 questions, 4 choices each, at least 16 correct (80 percent); wait one day to retake (handbook p. 18, p. 2).

Test languages: not stated in the handbook or on the DMV pages reached. The manual is published in Spanish (VN-007spa) and other languages; an interpreter is mentioned only for hearing-impaired applicants (p. 18).
No teen night-driving restriction in the handbook (p. 73 only suggests parents consider one).
Junior license: ages 16-17; state-approved driver education (30 h classroom, 6 h behind the wheel, 6 h observation) (p. 13). No driving for pay for 1 year; no passengers for hire (p. 15).
Speed: 50 mph maximum on all roads unless posted; Interstate 65 mph unless posted (p. 28).

Move over: slow down for stopped police/emergency/tow vehicles with lights; change lanes on a multilane road if safe (p. 31; p. 51 says slow to 20 mph below the limit if you cannot change lanes; 23 V.S.A. 1050).
School bus: stop while red lights flash; no stop on a divided highway for a bus going the other way (pp. 39-40; 23 V.S.A. 1075).
Points: 10 in two years starts suspension (p. 64; 23 V.S.A. 2505); lengths 10 pts = 10 days, 15 = 30, 20 = 90 (23 V.S.A. 2506, not in handbook).
Newer law than the handbook: 23 V.S.A. 1216 (under-21 0.02) was repealed by Act 45 of 2025, effective 2025-07-01; the rule is now 7 V.S.A. 656(b)(1)(E).
